bull_bear.body:
- Owns the land and buildings it develops - four generations of the Damani family have worked on this land and the campus is built on the Company's own former mill site
- Anchor lessee/licensee roster of established retail names - Star Bazaar, Westside, Zudio and Mr. DIY already trading, with Samsung, Adidas and Levi's commencing during the year, which lifts footfall and makes the campus more attractive to prospective lessees
- Integrated single-campus offering spanning retail, food, entertainment, hospitality, office space and wellness, which the Company expects to support higher footfall and create a differentiated destination in Solapur
- First-mover position in a Tier-II market - the Company committed to Solapur well before the property-consultant consensus on Tier-II retail arrived
- Asset base substantially constructed but not yet fully income-generating, so incremental leasing flows through with limited further construction cost; EBITDA of Rs. 370.70 lakhs was generated in FY 2025-26
- Adaptive reuse of over 80,000 square feet of existing mill structures rather than demolition and rebuilding, lowering development cost and environmental impact
- Demonstrated that technology-enabled services and back-office operations can be run from Solapur, evidenced by two managed centres with close to 500 seats serving Mahindra Integrated Business Solutions and Core Integra
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Single-city, single-campus concentration — MD&A Risks and Concerns states operations are concentrated in a single city and, substantially, on a single campus, exposing the Company to local economic conditions and the pace of development at Solapur. There is no geographic or asset diversification to absorb a downturn in that one market.
- Dependence on a limited number of anchor lessees/licensees — Performance is tied to a small set of anchors - Star Bazaar, Westside, Zudio and Mr. DIY - plus recently commenced brands. MD&A explicitly flags exposure to 'the performance of a limited number of anchor lessees/licensees', so the loss or underperformance of one anchor would materially affect footfall and rental income.
- Leverage and negative net worth - interest cover below one time — The Joint Managing Director discloses that finance costs of Rs. 290.36 lakhs equalled roughly 41 per cent of revenue from operations, that interest cover remained below one time through the year, and that net worth is negative as a result of accumulated losses. The Company has borrowed to fund development and is seeking shareholder approval to increase borrowing limits, so debt servicing depends on leasing income arriving on schedule.
- Asset base constructed ahead of the income it will produce — Management states the asset base is 'substantially constructed but not yet fully income-generating', with the FY26 loss arising only after depreciation of Rs. 94.20 lakhs on recently capitalised campus assets and finance costs on development borrowings. If committed lessees do not take possession and begin trading as expected, the gap between EBITDA and fixed charges does not close.
- Execution and timing risk on committed leasing and the Connplex Cinemas fit-out — Rentals from US Polo Assn., Arrow, Blackberrys, Jockey and Fastrack had not commenced at the year end and are only expected during FY 2026-27, and Connplex Cinemas remained work in progress. The expected improvement in revenue depends on these commencing on time.
- Competition from other developers and retail destinations, and shifting consumer preferences — Both the MD&A Threats section and Risks and Concerns flag competition from other developers and retail destinations and changes in consumer preferences. Retail destinations are moving to experience-led formats, so the campus must keep reinvesting in tenant mix and experience to hold footfall.
- Interest rate movements, government policy and regulatory approvals affecting development timing — MD&A lists interest rate movements, changes in government policy and regulatory approvals affecting the timing of development as market-related risks. Given the Company's leverage, rate movements feed directly into finance costs, and approval delays push out the income from the master-planned site.
- Dependence on Solapur's demand drivers - IT employment, brand expansion plans and connectivity — The MD&A states the pace of growth may be influenced by changes in IT employment trends, brand expansion plans, availability of skilled manpower and evolving market demand, and the Chairman describes connectivity as the single largest external opportunity. These are drivers outside the Company's control on which its co-working, office and retail plans rest.
- Listing-compliance lapses noted by the Secretarial Auditor — The MR-3 Secretarial Audit Report records a delay of one day in submission of the shareholding pattern for the quarter ended June 2025 and a delay in payment of listing fees under the SEBI LODR Regulations - minor, but the only qualifications raised in the compliance review.

business.body: The Company owns and develops real estate at a single campus in Solapur, Maharashtra, leasing retail, food, entertainment and office space to national and international brands and earning rental income from them. It also runs a hospitality business comprising Shubham Resort and Banquets and quick-service food formats on the campus, and hosts managed office centres for technology-enabled services clients. Reporting is on two segments, Property and Related Services and Hospitality Services, with the Company progressively shifting food and beverage from self-operation to third-party operators and lease rentals.

outlook.body:
- Monetise the Company's own land at Solapur by developing and leasing the Jamshri City campus, positioning it as an integrated commercial and lifestyle destination rather than a pure shopping format
- Build the business around Tier-II and Tier-III consumption, on the conviction that the next phase of India's organised retail growth belongs to smaller cities, with Solapur as the chosen base
- Attract reputed national and international brands as lessees/licensees, since their presence lifts footfall and strengthens the campus's appeal to further prospective occupiers
- Offer retail, food, entertainment, hospitality, office space and wellness facilities within a single campus to support higher footfall and create a differentiated destination in Solapur
- Shift hospitality from self-operated ventures to partnerships with proven hospitality operators, participating in food and beverage growth through lease rentals rather than direct operations - evidenced by the discontinuation of Swadisht Restaurant and expansion of QSR capacity via third-party operators
- Build a flexible workspace / co-working offering on the foundation of the two managed centres already running on campus, to attract IT and ITeS clients who wish to evaluate Solapur without committing to infrastructure of their own
- Convert the wider site vision into an approval-ready and commercially viable master plan through ANA, under Ar. Avinash Nawathe, appointed as master planner for Jamshri City
- Increase rental income and improve hospitality revenues while enhancing customer experience, so that operating income progressively covers depreciation and finance charges on the recently capitalised asset base
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company's entire expansion programme is the build-out of Jamshri City, a mixed-use development on its own land at Solapur bringing retail, lifestyle, hospitality, office space and community facilities into a single campus. During FY 2025-26 the Company borrowed for development activities including landscaping, roads, retail and office spaces, and states that the asset base is now substantially constructed but not yet fully income-generating, with the income benefit expected to arise in the coming years. Progress during the year: approximately 71,000 square feet of retail and commercial space stood occupied as of 31st March 2026, representing 70 per cent of the leasable area of Jamshri High Street; rentals commenced from Samsung, Adidas and Levi's alongside the anchor lessees/licensees Zudio, Star Bazaar, Westside and Mr. DIY; and over 80,000 square feet of existing mill structures were repurposed from warehouses into retail space with upgraded facades, energy-efficient systems and improved ventilation. The principal project still in progress is the fit-out of Connplex Cinemas, which stood as work in progress at the close of the financial year with box office, auditorium interiors, recliner seating and concession areas substantially complete, and which is expected to open and act as an entertainment anchor. For the wider site, the Company appointed ANA, under Ar. Avinash Nawathe, as master planner for Jamshri City to convert the vision into an approval-ready and commercially viable master plan, and that work continues. Leasing expansion continues alongside: agreements/LOIs were signed with US Polo, Arrow, Blackberry, Fastrack and Jockey for retail shops on 9-10 year terms covering approximately 6,000 sq ft, with rentals expected to commence during FY 2026-27. Two managed centres with close to 500 seats already run on campus for clients including Mahindra Integrated Business Solutions and Core Integra, and the Company intends to build a flexible workspace / co-working offering on that foundation to attract IT and ITeS clients to Solapur. Supporting campus infrastructure completed includes a 950 kW rooftop solar installation across 1,20,000 square feet, a rainwater harvesting scheme covering more than 60,000 square feet with restored campus wells providing storage of approximately 100 lakh litres, electric-vehicle charging points, and parking for more than 300 four-wheelers and 1000 two-wheelers. Funding flexibility for completing the development is being sought through a resolution at the Annual General Meeting to increase borrowing limits. The Company discloses no rupee capex quantum in this bundle.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Rental income growth as new lessees/licensees commence trading - rentals from Samsung, Adidas and Levi's commenced during the year and rentals from US Polo Assn., Arrow, Blackberrys, Jockey and Fastrack are expected to commence during FY 2026-27
- Management expects revenue to increase from the current financial year as committed lessees/licensees commence operations, and to continue working towards reducing the loss
- The asset base is substantially constructed but not yet fully income-generating; as leasing matures the Company expects operating income to progressively cover depreciation and finance costs
- Lower finance costs versus the preceding year, plus the discontinuation of the loss-making self-operated Swadisht Restaurant, were two of the three stated drivers of the improvement in results
- Expansion of organised retail into Tier-II and Tier-III cities, supported by rising disposable incomes, urbanisation and improving retail infrastructure, continuing to support demand for quality commercial, retail, food, entertainment and hospitality spaces
- Retail destinations moving beyond pure shopping formats towards experience-led offerings - food and beverage, entertainment, lifestyle, office space, wellness and community engagement - which management says aligns with the Company's integrated campus
- Tenant mix optimisation as a driver of successful retail and commercial properties, with reputed brands improving footfall and property positioning
- Improved air, rail and road connectivity for Solapur described as the single largest external opportunity, supporting higher visitor footfall and making the city more attractive to retail, hospitality, entertainment and office occupiers
- External corroboration cited by the Chairman: Cushman and Wakefield expects approximately 12.7 million square feet of mall supply to be delivered across tracked markets between 2026 and 2028, and CBRE attributes Tier-II retail real estate strength to economic expansion, infrastructure development, new business hubs, rising consumption and improved connectivity
- Macro backdrop cited: India's GDP grew 7.6% in FY 2025-26 with real GDP growth projected at approximately 6.9% and CPI inflation at around 4.6% for FY 2026-27; financial, real estate and professional services grew 9.9% and construction 7.1%
- Pace of growth may be influenced by changes in IT employment trends, brand expansion plans, availability of skilled manpower and evolving market demand
- Agreements/LOIs signed with US Polo, Arrow, Blackberry, Fastrack and Jockey for retail shops for a 9-10 year period covering an area of approximately 6,000 sq ft; rentals from these lessees/licensees are expected to commence during FY 2026-27 and did not contribute to FY 2025-26 results
- Over 70% of the leasable area of Jamshri High Street - approximately 71,000 square feet of retail and commercial space - stood let out as at 31st March 2026, leaving the balance available for leasing
- The Company executed further leasing agreements for space at its Solapur campus during the year and continued to receive enquiries from national brands evaluating the location
- Connplex Cinemas fit-out stood as work in progress at the close of the financial year, with box office, auditorium interiors, recliner seating and concession areas substantially complete, and is expected to open

currentContext.expansion: The Company's entire expansion programme is the build-out of Jamshri City, a mixed-use development on its own land at Solapur bringing retail, lifestyle, hospitality, office space and community facilities into a single campus. During FY 2025-26 the Company borrowed for development activities including landscaping, roads, retail and office spaces, and states that the asset base is now substantially constructed but not yet fully income-generating, with the income benefit expected to arise in the coming years. Progress during the year: approximately 71,000 square feet of retail and commercial space stood occupied as of 31st March 2026, representing 70 per cent of the leasable area of Jamshri High Street; rentals commenced from Samsung, Adidas and Levi's alongside the anchor lessees/licensees Zudio, Star Bazaar, Westside and Mr. DIY; and over 80,000 square feet of existing mill structures were repurposed from warehouses into retail space with upgraded facades, energy-efficient systems and improved ventilation. The principal project still in progress is the fit-out of Connplex Cinemas, which stood as work in progress at the close of the financial year with box office, auditorium interiors, recliner seating and concession areas substantially complete, and which is expected to open and act as an entertainment anchor. For the wider site, the Company appointed ANA, under Ar. Avinash Nawathe, as master planner for Jamshri City to convert the vision into an approval-ready and commercially viable master plan, and that work continues. Leasing expansion continues alongside: agreements/LOIs were signed with US Polo, Arrow, Blackberry, Fastrack and Jockey for retail shops on 9-10 year terms covering approximately 6,000 sq ft, with rentals expected to commence during FY 2026-27. Two managed centres with close to 500 seats already run on campus for clients including Mahindra Integrated Business Solutions and Core Integra, and the Company intends to build a flexible workspace / co-working offering on that foundation to attract IT and ITeS clients to Solapur. Supporting campus infrastructure completed includes a 950 kW rooftop solar installation across 1,20,000 square feet, a rainwater harvesting scheme covering more than 60,000 square feet with restored campus wells providing storage of approximately 100 lakh litres, electric-vehicle charging points, and parking for more than 300 four-wheelers and 1000 two-wheelers. Funding flexibility for completing the development is being sought through a resolution at the Annual General Meeting to increase borrowing limits. The Company discloses no rupee capex quantum in this bundle.

risks.note: MD&A Risks and Concerns states operations are concentrated in a single city and, substantially, on a single campus, exposing the Company to local economic conditions and the pace of development at Solapur. There is no geographic or asset diversification to absorb a downturn in that one market.

risks.risk: Dependence on a limited number of anchor lessees/licensees
risks.note: Performance is tied to a small set of anchors - Star Bazaar, Westside, Zudio and Mr. DIY - plus recently commenced brands. MD&A explicitly flags exposure to 'the performance of a limited number of anchor lessees/licensees', so the loss or underperformance of one anchor would materially affect footfall and rental income.

risks.risk: Leverage and negative net worth - interest cover below one time
risks.note: The Joint Managing Director discloses that finance costs of Rs. 290.36 lakhs equalled roughly 41 per cent of revenue from operations, that interest cover remained below one time through the year, and that net worth is negative as a result of accumulated losses. The Company has borrowed to fund development and is seeking shareholder approval to increase borrowing limits, so debt servicing depends on leasing income arriving on schedule.

risks.risk: Asset base constructed ahead of the income it will produce
risks.note: Management states the asset base is 'substantially constructed but not yet fully income-generating', with the FY26 loss arising only after depreciation of Rs. 94.20 lakhs on recently capitalised campus assets and finance costs on development borrowings. If committed lessees do not take possession and begin trading as expected, the gap between EBITDA and fixed charges does not close.

risks.risk: Execution and timing risk on committed leasing and the Connplex Cinemas fit-out
risks.note: Rentals from US Polo Assn., Arrow, Blackberrys, Jockey and Fastrack had not commenced at the year end and are only expected during FY 2026-27, and Connplex Cinemas remained work in progress. The expected improvement in revenue depends on these commencing on time.

risks.risk: Competition from other developers and retail destinations, and shifting consumer preferences
risks.note: Both the MD&A Threats section and Risks and Concerns flag competition from other developers and retail destinations and changes in consumer preferences. Retail destinations are moving to experience-led formats, so the campus must keep reinvesting in tenant mix and experience to hold footfall.

risks.risk: Interest rate movements, government policy and regulatory approvals affecting development timing
risks.note: MD&A lists interest rate movements, changes in government policy and regulatory approvals affecting the timing of development as market-related risks. Given the Company's leverage, rate movements feed directly into finance costs, and approval delays push out the income from the master-planned site.

risks.risk: Dependence on Solapur's demand drivers - IT employment, brand expansion plans and connectivity
risks.note: The MD&A states the pace of growth may be influenced by changes in IT employment trends, brand expansion plans, availability of skilled manpower and evolving market demand, and the Chairman describes connectivity as the single largest external opportunity. These are drivers outside the Company's control on which its co-working, office and retail plans rest.

risks.risk: Listing-compliance lapses noted by the Secretarial Auditor
risks.note: The MR-3 Secretarial Audit Report records a delay of one day in submission of the shareholding pattern for the quarter ended June 2025 and a delay in payment of listing fees under the SEBI LODR Regulations - minor, but the only qualifications raised in the compliance review.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Jamshri Realty Limited is a 118-year-old Solapur-based company that has converted its former mill land into Jamshri City, an integrated retail, hospitality, entertainment and office campus of which over 70% of the leasable area of Jamshri High Street was let out as at 31st March 2026.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company owns and develops real estate at a single campus in Solapur, Maharashtra, leasing retail, food, entertainment and office space to national and international brands and earning rental income from them. It also runs a hospitality business comprising Shubham Resort and Banquets and quick-service food formats on the campus, and hosts managed office centres for technology-enabled services clients. Reporting is on two segments, Property and Related Services and Hospitality Services, with the Company progressively shifting food and beverage from self-operation to third-party operators and lease rentals.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Property and Related Services:** Jamshri City (mixed-use development), Jamshri High Street (retail and commercial leasing), Managed office centres and proposed co-working offering, Office space leasing
- **Hospitality Services:** Shubham Resort and Banquets, Chaat pe Chacha (quick service format), Tidbit Cafe, Swadisht Restaurant (discontinued during FY 2025-26)

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Organised retail occupiers - national and international brands expanding into Tier-II and Tier-III cities
- Food and beverage and entertainment operators
- Hospitality, banqueting and events demand in Solapur
- IT / ITeS and back-office services clients evaluating Solapur
- Local and outstation visitor footfall in Solapur, Maharashtra

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Rental income growth as new lessees/licensees commence trading - rentals from Samsung, Adidas and Levi's commenced during the year and rentals from US Polo Assn., Arrow, Blackberrys, Jockey and Fastrack are expected to commence during FY 2026-27
- Management expects revenue to increase from the current financial year as committed lessees/licensees commence operations, and to continue working towards reducing the loss
- The asset base is substantially constructed but not yet fully income-generating; as leasing matures the Company expects operating income to progressively cover depreciation and finance costs
- Lower finance costs versus the preceding year, plus the discontinuation of the loss-making self-operated Swadisht Restaurant, were two of the three stated drivers of the improvement in results
- Expansion of organised retail into Tier-II and Tier-III cities, supported by rising disposable incomes, urbanisation and improving retail infrastructure, continuing to support demand for quality commercial, retail, food, entertainment and hospitality spaces
- Retail destinations moving beyond pure shopping formats towards experience-led offerings - food and beverage, entertainment, lifestyle, office space, wellness and community engagement - which management says aligns with the Company's integrated campus
- Tenant mix optimisation as a driver of successful retail and commercial properties, with reputed brands improving footfall and property positioning
- Improved air, rail and road connectivity for Solapur described as the single largest external opportunity, supporting higher visitor footfall and making the city more attractive to retail, hospitality, entertainment and office occupiers
- External corroboration cited by the Chairman: Cushman and Wakefield expects approximately 12.7 million square feet of mall supply to be delivered across tracked markets between 2026 and 2028, and CBRE attributes Tier-II retail real estate strength to economic expansion, infrastructure development, new business hubs, rising consumption and improved connectivity
- Macro backdrop cited: India's GDP grew 7.6% in FY 2025-26 with real GDP growth projected at approximately 6.9% and CPI inflation at around 4.6% for FY 2026-27; financial, real estate and professional services grew 9.9% and construction 7.1%
- Pace of growth may be influenced by changes in IT employment trends, brand expansion plans, availability of skilled manpower and evolving market demand
- Agreements/LOIs signed with US Polo, Arrow, Blackberry, Fastrack and Jockey for retail shops for a 9-10 year period covering an area of approximately 6,000 sq ft; rentals from these lessees/licensees are expected to commence during FY 2026-27 and did not contribute to FY 2025-26 results
- Over 70% of the leasable area of Jamshri High Street - approximately 71,000 square feet of retail and commercial space - stood let out as at 31st March 2026, leaving the balance available for leasing
- The Company executed further leasing agreements for space at its Solapur campus during the year and continued to receive enquiries from national brands evaluating the location
- Connplex Cinemas fit-out stood as work in progress at the close of the financial year, with box office, auditorium interiors, recliner seating and concession areas substantially complete, and is expected to open

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Monetise the Company's own land at Solapur by developing and leasing the Jamshri City campus, positioning it as an integrated commercial and lifestyle destination rather than a pure shopping format
- Build the business around Tier-II and Tier-III consumption, on the conviction that the next phase of India's organised retail growth belongs to smaller cities, with Solapur as the chosen base
- Attract reputed national and international brands as lessees/licensees, since their presence lifts footfall and strengthens the campus's appeal to further prospective occupiers
- Offer retail, food, entertainment, hospitality, office space and wellness facilities within a single campus to support higher footfall and create a differentiated destination in Solapur
- Shift hospitality from self-operated ventures to partnerships with proven hospitality operators, participating in food and beverage growth through lease rentals rather than direct operations - evidenced by the discontinuation of Swadisht Restaurant and expansion of QSR capacity via third-party operators
- Build a flexible workspace / co-working offering on the foundation of the two managed centres already running on campus, to attract IT and ITeS clients who wish to evaluate Solapur without committing to infrastructure of their own
- Convert the wider site vision into an approval-ready and commercially viable master plan through ANA, under Ar. Avinash Nawathe, appointed as master planner for Jamshri City
- Increase rental income and improve hospitality revenues while enhancing customer experience, so that operating income progressively covers depreciation and finance charges on the recently capitalised asset base
